quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: On roadways, bicycles are considered:

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles on roadways. Bicyclists and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: You need extra space in front of a large truck for:

options.text: Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.
The truck to stop.
Other drivers to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck to stop.
questions.explanation: Trucks take longer to stop than cars at the same speed. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beam headlights. If visibility is very poor, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: When driving on snow or ice:

options.text: It is safe to use cruise control.
Change speed and direction more slowly than usual.
Drive as you would on normal roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change speed and direction more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: On snow or ice, make slow changes to speed and direction. Never use cruise control on snow or ice because your tires may lose grip and you could lose control.

questions.question: Driving at night is more dangerous than driving during the day because:

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead.
The road is always more slippery at night.
Your reaction time is slower.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead.
questions.explanation: At night, you see less far ahead due to darkness and glare from oncoming headlights. Always use headlights and drive carefully in the dark.

questions.question: This white sign means you should not pass other vehicles:

options.text: Until after you pass the sign.
Unless it seems safe.
For any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: For any reason.
questions.explanation: White rectangular signs are mandatory rules. This sign means do not pass other vehicles under any circumstances.

questions.question: You should leave extra space when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space behind motorcycles because they stop faster than other vehicles. You need room to stop if the motorcycle brakes suddenly. Motorcycles are also hard to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: After a minor collision with no injuries and little damage, you should:

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if possible.
Not move your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if possible.
questions.explanation: After a minor collision with no injuries, move your vehicle out of traffic if you can do so safely.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, you should drive at:

options.text: The same speed as freeway traffic.
The posted speed limit.
A slower speed than freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Enter the freeway at the same speed as traffic unless traffic exceeds the legal speed limit.

questions.question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection with no oncoming vehicles.
Where signs and road markings allow passing.
In a curve with no oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where signs and road markings allow passing.
questions.explanation: Never pass at intersections, parking lot entrances, or alleys. Do not pass on curves or hills where you cannot see oncoming traffic. Only pass where signs and markings permit it and where you have enough space to pass safely.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Stop for other traffic.
Traffic is entering from another road. Give extra space so drivers can merge safely.
Traffic is entering from another road. Keep right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is entering from another road. Give extra space so drivers can merge safely.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic is merging into your lane. Check your mirrors and move to another lane if possible to give merging drivers clear space.

questions.question: Alcohol in any amount is:

options.text: A stimulant.
A depressant.
Neither.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows nerve impulses and body functions. It reduces inhibitions and makes it harder to focus and stay alert.

questions.question: At a "Yield" sign, you must:

options.text: Yield to traffic that is close enough to cause an accident.
Yield only to vehicles on your right.
Always slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic that is close enough to cause an accident.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Give the right of way to any crossing or merging traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on the highway, you should:

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Park with all four wheels off the road, if possible.
Stop where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park with all four wheels off the road, if possible.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, park completely off the road if you can.

questions.question: When backing up:

options.text: Look out the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Use only your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look out the rear window.
questions.explanation: When backing up, put your right arm on the passenger seat and look directly through the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors since they do not show the area directly behind your vehicle. Back up slowly.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass if you are in the lane next to the solid yellow line.
No one can pass from either direction.
You can pass if you are in the lane next to the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass if you are in the lane next to the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. If a broken line is next to your lane, you can cross it to pass. If a solid line is next to your lane, you cannot cross it.

questions.question: How do you see vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Use the outside rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. You must turn and look over your shoulders to see these areas.

questions.question: What must you do when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights?

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.
questions.explanation: Pull your vehicle to the right edge of the road and stop. Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle passes.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drugs and driving?

options.text: Prescription drugs are safe if you don't feel drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs can make you unsafe to drive.
Only illegal drugs affect driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over-the-counter drugs can make you unsafe to drive.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can harm your ability to drive safely. This includes drugs for colds, allergies, and anxiety. Any drug that affects your driving is illegal to use before driving.

questions.question: When can you pass on the right shoulder of the road?

options.text: When the car in front is turning.
When the car in front is driving slowly.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You cannot drive on the shoulder of the road. Do not pass on the shoulder under any circumstances.

questions.question: You hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.
questions.explanation: You must leave a written note attached to the vehicle with your name, phone number, and address.

questions.question: What do yellow lines separate?

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of roads with traffic moving in both directions. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. A broken yellow line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do if you encounter a severe dust storm?

options.text: Slow down and pull off the road.
Turn on your high beams.
Keep your speed and stay in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Slow down and drive completely off the road to the right. Stop as far right as possible. Turn off your lights, keep your foot off the brake, and stay in your vehicle with your seat belt on until the storm passes.

questions.question: When can you cross double yellow lines to pass?

options.text: When the car in front moves right to let you pass.
When the yellow line next to your side is broken.
When the yellow line next to the other side is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the yellow line next to your side is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass if it is safe. A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red light?

options.text: Slow down and yield.
Slow down and drive carefully through.
Stop completely, check traffic, and go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check traffic, and go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light is the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for other traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What is the thinking of a defensive driver?

options.text: Other drivers will do the right thing.
Other drivers might make mistakes, so I prepare to react.
I expect no favors and give none.

questions.correctAnswerText: Other drivers might make mistakes, so I prepare to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you expect other drivers to make mistakes and you are ready to react safely to avoid problems.

questions.question: Driving slower than surrounding traffic is:

options.text: Good if the weather is bad.
OK if you don't know the speed limit.
Dangerous because other drivers may try to pass you recklessly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous because other drivers may try to pass you recklessly.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic frustrates other drivers. They may take dangerous risks to pass you.

questions.question: How do stopping distance and crash severity change with speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
Speed does not affect them.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds cause longer stopping distances and more severe crashes.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid losing traction on wet roads?

options.text: Make sharp turns.
Brake hard.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down on wet roads to prevent hydroplaning. Keep your tires in good condition. If you lose control, take your foot off the gas, do not brake, and keep the vehicle straight until it slows.

questions.question: What should you do when bright headlights are coming toward you at night?

options.text: Stop until the other car passes.
Look below the headlights.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes.
